summary: High-quality Pt thin films are deposited using atomic layer deposition (ALD) with dimethyl-(N,N-dimethyl-3-butene-1amine-N) platinum (C8H19NPt) and diluted molecular oxygen (O2) as reactants. The process shows self-limiting growth characteristics and a well-defined ALD temperature window between 200 and 250 °C. The films exhibit high growth per cycle (0.167 nm) and excellent conformality, with resistivity values close to bulk resistivity. The study compares ALD-Pt with ALD-Ru, highlighting the superior electrical properties of ALD-Pt due to larger grain size and high purity.
evidence: High-quality Pt thin films are prepared by atomic layer deposition (ALD) using metal-organic precursors dimethyl-(N,N-dimethyl-3-butene-1amine-N) platinum (C8H19NPt) and with diluted molecular oxygen (O2) as a reactant. The films are grown at a relatively low temperature of 225 °C on a thermally grown SiO2 substrate, and the process shows all the necessary qualities of an ideal ALD such as self-limiting growth characteristics and a well-defined ALD temperature window between 200 and 250 °C. Noticeably, the current ALD-Pt process shows a very high growth per cycle of 0.167 nm without an incubation period at 225 °C, and perfect conformality is obtained at a dual trench structure (top and bottom width: 40 and 15 nm) with an aspect ratio of around 6.3. The resistivity of the ALD-Pt film at ∼39 nm in thickness deposited at 225 °C is almost the same (∼10.8 μΩ cm) as its bulk resistivity (10.6 μΩ cm), and it is as low as ∼12 μΩ cm at 25 nm in thickness. Comprehensive analyses using x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, x-ray diffractometry, transmission electron microscopy (TEM), and x-ray reflectance indicate that the extremely low resistivity of ALD-Pt is due to the formation of highly pure and polycrystalline films with high density (∼21.04 g/cm3) and large grain size (∼48 nm for 25 nm thick film).
